#!/bin/sh
### General options

### LSF (-q gpua100) -> SLURM (--partition=gpua100)
#SBATCH --partition=gpua100

### LSF (-gpu "num=1:mode=exclusive_process") -> SLURM (--gpus=1)
#SBATCH --gpus=1
# NOTE: The LSF 'mode=exclusive_process' is often the default behavior in SLURM when a full GPU is requested.
# This can be site-specific, but --gpus=1 typically reserves the device exclusively for the job.

### LSF (-J run_bert_fremstillingsform) -> SLURM (--job-name=run_bert_fremstillingsform)
#SBATCH --job-name=run_bert_fremstillingsform

### LSF (-n 4 & -R "span[hosts=1]") -> SLURM (--nodes=1 --ntasks=1 --cpus-per-task=4)
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4

### LSF (-R "rusage[mem=12GB]") -> SLURM (--mem=12G)
#SBATCH --mem=12G

### LSF (-W 24:00) -> SLURM (--time=24:00:00)
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00

### LSF (-N) -> SLURM (--mail-type=END)
#SBATCH --mail-type=END
# please uncomment the following line and put in your e-mail address,
# if you want to receive e-mail notifications on a non-default address
##SBATCH --mail-user=your_email_address
# NOTE: The original LSF script also had a commented-out option for email on job start (-B).
# To receive emails on both start and end, use: #SBATCH --mail-type=BEGIN,END

### LSF (-oo) -> SLURM (--output)
#SBATCH --output=./out_files/BERT/BERT_Fremstillingsform.out

### LSF (-eo) -> SLURM (--error)
#SBATCH --error=./out_files/BERT/BERT_Fremstillingsform.err

# here follow the commands you want to execute

# Load dependencies
module load python3/3.9.14
#module load gcc/10.3.0
#module load cuda/11.5
module load cudnn/v8.3.0.98-prod-cuda-11.5

source ./venv/bin/activate
# echo $VIRTUAL_ENV

python3 run_BERT_finetune.py --target_col "Fremstillingsform"

issues: The script uses relative paths for output/error files ('./out_files/...') and the virtual environment ('./venv'). This can lead to errors if the job is not submitted from the intended directory. It is safer to use absolute paths or SLURM environment variables like '$SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR'.

The output and error file paths ('./out_files/BERT/') imply a directory structure that may not exist. The job could fail if it cannot create these files. It's recommended to add a 'mkdir -p ./out_files/BERT' command at the beginning of the execution block to ensure the target directory exists.

#!/bin/sh 
### General options 
### -- specify queue -- 
#BSUB -q gpua100
#BSUB -gpu "num=1:mode=exclusive_process"
### -- set the job Name -- 
#BSUB -J run_bert_fremstillingsform
### -- ask for number of cores (default: 1) -- 
#BSUB -n 4
### -- specify that the cores must be on the same host -- 
#BSUB -R "span[hosts=1]"
### -- specify that we need 2GB of memory per core/slot -- 
#BSUB -R "rusage[mem=12GB]"
### -- set walltime limit: hh:mm -- 
#BSUB -W 24:00 
### -- set the email address -- 
# please uncomment the following line and put in your e-mail address,
# if you want to receive e-mail notifications on a non-default address
##BSUB -u your_email_address
### -- send notification at start -- 
##BSUB -B 
### -- send notification at completion -- 
#BSUB -N 
### -- Specify the output and error file. %J is the job-id -- 
### -- -o and -e mean append, -oo and -eo mean overwrite -- 
#BSUB -oo ./out_files/BERT/BERT_Fremstillingsform.out
#BSUB -eo ./out_files/BERT/BERT_Fremstillingsform.err

# here follow the commands you want to execute 

# Load dependencies
module load python3/3.9.14
#module load gcc/10.3.0
#module load cuda/11.5
module load cudnn/v8.3.0.98-prod-cuda-11.5

source ./venv/bin/activate
# echo $VIRTUAL_ENV

python3 run_BERT_finetune.py --target_col "Fremstillingsform"
